“Hear about all these too,” he says. “The stones taken up from the plain and placed in the tower’s building in place of the rejected stones are the roots of this white mountain.”

2. “Since all the believers from this mountain were found innocent, the Lord of the tower ordered that these stones from the mountain’s roots be put into the tower’s building. For he knew that if these stones went into the building, they would remain bright, and not one of them would turn black.”

3. “But if he had added stones from the other mountains, he would have had to inspect that tower again and purify it. All these, however, were found white,[a] both those who have believed and those who will believe. For they are of the same kind.[b] Blessed is this kind, because it is innocent.”

4. “Now hear also about those round and splendid stones. They are all from this white mountain. Hear why they were found round. Their riches have darkened them a little with respect to the truth and clouded them. Yet they never departed from God, nor did any evil word come from their mouths, but only righteousness and the virtue of truth.”

5. “When the Lord saw their disposition—that they could favor the truth[c] and also remain good—he ordered their wealth to be cut back, rather than taken away entirely. Then they could do some good with what was left to them, and they will live to God, because they are of a good kind. So they were trimmed a little and placed in the structure of this tower.”

base_translation:
  text: '“Hear about all these too,” he says. “The stones taken up from the plain and placed in the tower’s
    building in place of the rejected stones are the roots of this white mountain.”


    2. “Since all the believers from this mountain were found innocent, the Lord of the tower ordered
    that these stones from the mountain’s roots be put into the tower’s building. For he knew that if
    these stones went into the building, they would remain bright, and not one of them would turn black.”


    3. “But if he had added stones from the other mountains, he would have had to inspect that tower again
    and purify it. All these, however, were found white,[a] both those who have believed and those who
    will believe. For they are of the same kind.[b] Blessed is this kind, because it is innocent.”


    4. “Now hear also about those round and splendid stones. They are all from this white mountain. Hear
    why they were found round. Their riches have darkened them a little with respect to the truth and
    clouded them. Yet they never departed from God, nor did any evil word come from their mouths, but
    only righteousness and the virtue of truth.”


    5. “When the Lord saw their disposition—that they could favor the truth[c] and also remain good—he
    ordered their wealth to be cut back, rather than taken away entirely. Then they could do some good
    with what was left to them, and they will live to God, because they are of a good kind. So they were
    trimmed a little and placed in the structure of this tower.”'
